issues.description: The problem statement's UML and the solution expect a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) but the template Stock class provides addItem(StockIngredient) instead. This name/signature mismatch is structural: students following the specification or the solution example will attempt to call addToStockIngredients and find no such method in the template, causing compile errors or confusion about whether to rename or add methods in Stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the method addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) to the template Stock class (or rename the existing addItem to addToStockIngredients) so the template matches the UML and the solution. Optionally keep addItem as a delegating alias to preserve backwards compatibility: public void addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient ing) { addItem(ing); }

issues.description: The Stock API name for adding a StockIngredient differs between artifacts: the problem statement (and the solution) specify addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template implementation provides addItem(StockIngredient). This mismatch can confuse students implementing SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery or following the class diagram because the expected method name from the exercise description does not exist in the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or add an alias method with the expected name) so that the template matches the problem statement's API and the solution implementation. Alternatively, update the problem statement and solution to use addItem consistently.
